dedup.scope: Same-source public primary and the claim already prepared from this source, plus the public identity index, the retired-claims record and the current worklist searched with the object names separated set, bounded degree Borel graph, hyperfinite, sufficiently separated cover, topological Ramsey space and comeager.

compared.difference: Same source, different proposition: l:indep2 (source lines 540-550) starts from one bounded-degree Borel graph on the Ellentuck space and finds a cone [A'] on which the graph is contained in eventual equality. There is no sequence of graphs, no separated family B_n and no hyperfiniteness conclusion.

Counts the article's main theorem t:ramsey hyperfin (source lines 412-414, restated at 645-647), which is obtained by applying the present theorem to the separated covers built in Lemma ramsey separation. The present statement is therefore upstream of that one and is not one of its corollaries; the two have different hypotheses (a bounded-degree decomposition plus separated Borel sets versus a topological Ramsey space) and different objects.

compared.difference: Near neighbours returned were 210058 (arxiv:2609.11866:prop:semiselective.implies.mathias, every subset of a topological Ramsey space is Ramsey in the Solovay model), 168479 (arxiv:2411.08797:pr:fihtocov, complexity of finite Borel asymptotic dimension), 185286 (arxiv:2509.15000:lem-technical, measurable one-ended spanning trees), 184578 (arxiv:2509.05548:closed, hyperfiniteness of boundary actions) and 210571 (arxiv:2609.17177:thm-main, bounded-to-one commutative monoid actions). None of them states that a bounded-degree decomposition plus a separated family covering every point infinitely often forces hyperfiniteness on the covered set.
